source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — The Living World
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: In binomial nomenclature, the first word of a biological name represents the
questions.explanation: The scientific name is Genus + specific epithet; the first word is the genus.

questions.stem: In the taxonomic hierarchy, a family is an assemblage of related
questions.explanation: Related genera are grouped into a family.

questions.stem: Organisms capable of interbreeding to produce fertile offspring are placed in the same
questions.explanation: A biological species is a group of organisms that interbreed and yield fertile young.

questions.stem: Dried and pressed plant specimens mounted on sheets and stored for study constitute a
questions.explanation: A herbarium is a storehouse of dried, pressed and labelled plant specimens.

questions.stem: Kew (Royal Botanic Gardens) is an internationally famous example of a
questions.explanation: Kew maintains living plants for study, conservation and reference.

questions.stem: A taxonomic key that offers two contrasting choices at each step is called a
questions.explanation: Dichotomous keys identify an organism by successive couplets of opposite characters.

questions.stem: Scientific names of plants are assigned according to the rules of the
questions.explanation: Plant names follow the International Code of Botanical Nomenclature (now ICN).

questions.stem: Systematics differs from taxonomy mainly because it also studies
questions.explanation: Taxonomy is identification, naming and classification; systematics also includes phylogeny.

questions.stem: Isolated metabolic reactions in a test tube are not called living systems because they lack
questions.explanation: Metabolism of life occurs inside cells; a cell-free reaction mixture is not an organism.

questions.stem: The process of giving a scientific name to a newly discovered organism is called
questions.explanation: Nomenclature is the assignment of a unique scientific name.

questions.stem: In the name Mangifera indica, the word indica denotes the
questions.explanation: Mangifera is the genus; indica is the specific epithet of mango.

questions.stem: Among species, genus, family and order, the highest taxonomic rank is
questions.explanation: Rank rises as species → genus → family → order.

questions.stem: The family to which mango (Mangifera indica) belongs is
questions.explanation: Mango is placed in family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales.

questions.stem: A correctly written biological name in a printed paper should have the
options: genus and specific epithet both italicised
genus italicised and the epithet in roman
family name placed before the genus
questions.explanation: Both words of the binomial are italicised (or underlined if handwritten).

questions.stem: Which taxonomic category includes all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: Kingdom is the highest of these ranks and contains many orders, families and genera.

questions.stem: The most specific (lowest) taxonomic category among the following is
questions.explanation: Species is the lowest rank and the basic unit of classification.

questions.stem: Herbarium sheets are mainly useful for
questions.explanation: Pressed labelled sheets are a reference collection for plant identification.

questions.stem: Which taxonomic aid maintains living plant specimens with scientific labels?
questions.explanation: Botanical gardens grow living plants; herbaria store dried sheets.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not regarded as a taxonomic aid?
questions.explanation: Herbarium, garden, museum and key are taxonomic aids; a spectrophotometer is a lab instrument.

questions.stem: The International Code of Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN) lays down rules for naming
questions.explanation: ICZN governs scientific names of animals; plants follow ICBN/ICN.

questions.stem: Taxonomy is a part of systematics. Systematics additionally includes the study of
questions.explanation: Systematics = taxonomy plus the evolutionary history of taxa.

questions.stem: Growth cannot be used as a unique defining feature of living organisms because
options: non-living objects can also increase in mass by accumulation
animals do not grow after birth
questions.explanation: Mountains, boulders and sand dunes also 'grow' by adding material from outside.

questions.stem: Scientific names are preferred over common names because they are
options: changed every year by each country
questions.explanation: One organism has one scientific name used worldwide, unlike many local common names.

questions.stem: When a biological name is handwritten, each of the two words should be
questions.explanation: Handwritten binomials are underlined separately; printed ones are italicised.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect pair of taxonomic rank and example.
questions.explanation: Poaceae is a family (grasses), not a class. Mango: genus Mangifera, family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales.

questions.stem: Taxonomic keys used for identification are based on
options: the year the organism was discovered
questions.explanation: A key is a couplet of opposite characters leading the user to the next step or the name.
